quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: Careful and tactful when dealing with sensitive situations, especially between people.
quests.explanation: Diplomatic describes skilful, tactful handling of a delicate situation. This quality is valuable both in international relations and everyday conversation.
quests.textToSpeak: She handled the awkward question in a very diplomatic way.
quests.textWithBlanks: She handled the awkward question in a very ___ way.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: The past form of 'boycott' — to refuse to buy from or deal with a company as a form of protest.
quests.explanation: Boycotted means deliberately avoided as a form of protest. This is a common consumer response to companies seen as behaving badly.
quests.textToSpeak: Consumers boycotted the brand after the scandal became public.
quests.textWithBlanks: Consumers ___ the brand after the scandal became public.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: Started by ordinary people at a local level, rather than by leaders or organisations.
quests.explanation: Grassroots describes something starting from ordinary people rather than from the top. 'One neighbourhood' shows just how locally and modestly it began.
quests.textToSpeak: The campaign began as a small grassroots movement in one neighbourhood.
quests.textWithBlanks: The campaign began as a small ___ movement in one neighbourhood.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: The past form of 'consolidate' — to combine separate things into one, usually stronger, unit.
quests.explanation: Consolidated means combined into a single, often stronger unit. Companies often do this to cut costs or work more efficiently.
quests.textToSpeak: The two departments consolidated into a single, larger team.
quests.textWithBlanks: The two departments ___ into a single, larger team.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: Able to govern or manage itself independently, without outside control.
quests.explanation: Autonomous describes independence in decision-making, often used about regions or systems. 'Its own education system' shows exactly what this independence covered.
quests.textToSpeak: The region was granted autonomous control over its own education system.
quests.textWithBlanks: The region was granted ___ control over its own education system.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: A strong negative reaction from a large number of people.
quests.explanation: Backlash describes a strong wave of public anger or criticism. 'Cancelling the popular feature' explains exactly what triggered it.
quests.textToSpeak: The company faced a huge backlash after cancelling the popular feature.
quests.textWithBlanks: The company faced a huge ___ after cancelling the popular feature.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: The past form of 'circumvent' — to find a legal or clever way around a rule or difficulty.
quests.explanation: Circumvented means found a way around an obstacle, often a rule. Opening a local factory is a clever, legal way to avoid an import tax.
quests.textToSpeak: The company circumvented the new import tax by opening a local factory.
quests.textWithBlanks: The company ___ the new import tax by opening a local factory.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: Not based on any facts or evidence; without real support.
quests.explanation: Unfounded describes claims with no factual basis behind them. 'Turned out to be' shows this was only confirmed after some genuine doubt.
quests.textToSpeak: The rumours about the merger turned out to be completely unfounded.
quests.textWithBlanks: The rumours about the merger turned out to be completely ___.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: A wealthy person who generously gives money to good causes.
quests.explanation: A philanthropist is someone who donates significant money or time to charitable causes. 'Most of his fortune' shows an unusually generous level of giving.
quests.textToSpeak: The billionaire philanthropist donated most of his fortune to medical research.
quests.textWithBlanks: The billionaire ___ donated most of his fortune to medical research.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: An earlier decision or action used as an example or guide for later, similar situations.
quests.explanation: Precedent is a past decision that guides future ones in similar situations. This word is central to how legal systems build consistency over time.
quests.textToSpeak: The ruling set an important legal precedent for future cases.
quests.textWithBlanks: The ruling set an important legal ___ for future cases.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: Disappointed after realising something is not as good as you once believed.
quests.explanation: Disillusioned describes disappointment after losing faith in something once trusted. 'Mainstream politics' shows the specific area of this disappointment.
quests.textToSpeak: Many young voters felt disillusioned with mainstream politics.
quests.textWithBlanks: Many young voters felt ___ with mainstream politics.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: Something that causes an important change or event to happen.
quests.explanation: A catalyst triggers significant change, often unexpectedly. Documentaries occasionally have exactly this kind of real-world impact.
quests.textToSpeak: The documentary became a catalyst for real changes in fishing laws.
quests.textWithBlanks: The documentary became a ___ for real changes in fishing laws.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: The past form of 'scrutinise' — to examine something very closely and carefully.
quests.explanation: Scrutinised means examined in close, careful detail. Budgets are commonly scrutinised before being officially approved.
quests.textToSpeak: Every expense was carefully scrutinised before the budget was approved.
quests.textWithBlanks: Every expense was carefully ___ before the budget was approved.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: Very persuasive and interesting, in a way that grabs your full attention.
quests.explanation: Compelling describes an argument or story so persuasive it's hard to ignore. 'Convinced the jury' shows exactly how effective it was.
quests.textToSpeak: The lawyer presented a compelling argument that convinced the jury.
quests.textWithBlanks: The lawyer presented a ___ argument that convinced the jury.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: Having a great deal of money; wealthy.
quests.explanation: Affluent describes wealth, often used about people, areas, or society generally. The comparison with the capital highlights a real economic inequality.
quests.textToSpeak: The charity works mainly in areas that are far less affluent than the capital.
quests.textWithBlanks: The charity works mainly in areas that are far less ___ than the capital.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: A temporary alliance between different groups, often to achieve a shared goal.
quests.explanation: Coalition describes a group of parties or organisations working together, often in politics. This usually happens when no single group has enough power alone.
quests.textToSpeak: Several small parties formed a coalition to govern together.
quests.textWithBlanks: Several small parties formed a ___ to govern together.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: The past form of 'exploit' — to treat someone unfairly for your own benefit or profit.
quests.explanation: Exploited means used someone unfairly for personal or business gain. 'Extremely low wages' shows exactly how the workers were being treated unfairly.
quests.textToSpeak: The factory was accused of exploited workers with extremely low wages.
quests.textWithBlanks: The factory was accused of ___ workers with extremely low wages.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: The quality of being honest and having strong moral principles.
quests.explanation: Integrity describes consistent honesty and strong moral character. 'Even by her critics' shows this quality was recognised by everyone, not just supporters.
quests.textToSpeak: Her integrity was never once questioned, even by her critics.
quests.textWithBlanks: Her ___ was never once questioned, even by her critics.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: The past form of 'unveil' — to show or reveal something publicly for the first time.
quests.explanation: Unveiled means officially revealed something new to the public. Press conferences are a classic setting for unveiling new products.
quests.textToSpeak: The company unveiled its latest product at a press conference.
quests.textWithBlanks: The company ___ its latest product at a press conference.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: Relating to what is morally right or wrong in how something is done.
quests.explanation: Ethical concerns whether something is done in a morally acceptable way. 'Sourcing of their clothes' points to a specific, common modern concern.
quests.textToSpeak: More shoppers are asking questions about the ethical sourcing of their clothes.
quests.textWithBlanks: More shoppers are asking questions about the ___ sourcing of their clothes.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: A person blamed for something, even though they may not really be responsible.
quests.explanation: A scapegoat takes the blame for others' mistakes. 'Problems he hadn't caused' makes clear that this blame was unfair.
quests.textToSpeak: He felt he was being made a scapegoat for problems he hadn't caused.
quests.textWithBlanks: He felt he was being made a ___ for problems he hadn't caused.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: A turning point that marks a significant and lasting change.
quests.explanation: Watershed describes a decisive turning point after which things are noticeably different. 'In the country's history' shows the scale of significance being claimed.
quests.textToSpeak: The election was described as a watershed moment in the country's history.
quests.textWithBlanks: The election was described as a ___ moment in the country's history.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: So important or useful that a situation cannot succeed without it.
quests.explanation: Indispensable describes something or someone essential, impossible to do without. This is one of the strongest compliments you can pay a colleague.
quests.textToSpeak: Her experience made her indispensable to the success of the project.
quests.textWithBlanks: Her experience made her ___ to the success of the project.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: Not securely fixed or safe; likely to become worse at any moment.
quests.explanation: Precarious describes instability, often financial or physical. Freelance work is frequently discussed using exactly this word, given its unpredictable income.
quests.textToSpeak: Many freelancers face a genuinely precarious financial situation.
quests.textWithBlanks: Many freelancers face a genuinely ___ financial situation.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: The past form of 'mitigate' — to make something bad less severe or serious.
quests.explanation: Mitigated means reduced the seriousness of a negative situation. 'Quick action by engineers' shows exactly what caused this improvement.
quests.textToSpeak: Quick action by engineers mitigated the worst effects of the flood.
quests.textWithBlanks: Quick action by engineers ___ the worst effects of the flood.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: Divided into two strongly opposing groups, with little middle ground.
quests.explanation: Polarised describes opinion splitting into two opposing extremes. 'Increasingly... over the years' shows this was a gradual process, not a sudden one.
quests.textToSpeak: Public opinion on the issue became increasingly polarised over the years.
quests.textWithBlanks: Public opinion on the issue became increasingly ___ over the years.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: The lasting impact or influence someone leaves behind after they are gone or finished.
quests.explanation: Legacy describes what someone is remembered for after their time ends. Healthcare reforms are exactly the kind of lasting impact this word describes.
quests.textToSpeak: The president's legacy includes major reforms to the healthcare system.
quests.textWithBlanks: The president's ___ includes major reforms to the healthcare system.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: The past form of 'underpin' — to form the basis or support for something.
quests.explanation: Underpinned means formed the essential foundation supporting something else. This word is common when describing what makes a system or argument stable.
quests.textToSpeak: Strong customer trust underpinned the bank's entire business model.
quests.textWithBlanks: Strong customer trust ___ the bank's entire business model.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: Perfect and without any faults or mistakes.
quests.explanation: Impeccable describes flawless quality, with no faults at all. 'From start to finish' shows this high standard stayed consistent throughout.
quests.textToSpeak: The waiter's service was impeccable from start to finish.
quests.textWithBlanks: The waiter's service was ___ from start to finish.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and type the missing word.
quests.hint: Describes one event triggering a whole chain of further, similar events.
quests.explanation: Domino, in the phrase 'domino effect,' describes one event triggering a connected chain of further events. A single factory closing can set off exactly this kind of wider economic chain reaction.
quests.textToSpeak: One factory closure created a domino effect across the whole local economy.
quests.textWithBlanks: One factory closure created a ___ effect across the whole local economy.
